title: Which other angles make a triangle with these four angles?
description: For each of four angles, the video takes the angle away from one hundred and eighty to find the limit, then picks two other angles that make a triangle and two that do not. The method is the same as the example in the book.
teaching_notes: One idea: a second angle makes a triangle only when it is less than one hundred and eighty minus the first angle. Watch for students who count the limit angle itself as one that works.

source: For each of the following angles, find another angle for which a triangle is (a) possible, (b) not possible. Find at least two different angles for each category: (i) 30° (ii) 70° (iii) 54° (iv) 144°
video_script.why: The child can find the smallest second angle that stops the arms meeting for one angle and now does it for four angles.
video_script.substitution: Take the given angle away from one hundred and eighty to find the limit, then pick angles below it and angles at or above it.
video_script.anchor: four angles: thirty, seventy, fifty four and one hundred and forty four degrees
video_script.payoff_line: Any other angle below one hundred and eighty degrees minus the given angle makes a triangle

final_answer.value: 30°: possible 40°, 100°; not possible 150°, 170°. 70°: possible 20°, 100°; not possible 110°, 130°. 54°: possible 30°, 120°; not possible 126°, 150°. 144°: possible 10°, 30°; not possible 36°, 90°
final_answer.spoken: any other angle below one hundred and eighty degrees minus the given angle makes a triangle, and the examples are thirty with forty, one hundred and one hundred and fifty, and so on

maths_rules: the arm from the other end that leans least and does not meet is parallel to the first arm, so the two angles add to 180°
30°: 180° - 30° = 150°, so any other angle below 150° makes a triangle (for example 40°, 100°) and 150° or more does not (150°, 170°)
video_script.design: The four given angles stay in the anchor band. One number line per angle shows the limit, with the working angles in green on the left and the failing angles in red from the limit onwards.

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step one, use the rule from the example in your book. The arm that leans least and does not meet is parallel to the first arm.
<bookmark mark='limit'/>Then the two angles add to one hundred and eighty degrees. The limit is one hundred and eighty minus the given angle.
<bookmark mark='a'/>Step two, take each angle away from one hundred and eighty. One hundred and eighty minus thirty is one hundred and fifty.
<bookmark mark='b'/>One hundred and eighty minus seventy is one hundred and ten.
<bookmark mark='c'/>One hundred and eighty minus fifty four is one hundred and twenty six.
<bookmark mark='d'/>One hundred and eighty minus one hundred and forty four is thirty six.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: for each angle pick two angles below its limit, which make a triangle, and two angles at the limit or above it, which do not

narration: <bookmark mark='below'/>Step three, for each angle pick two angles below its limit. These make a triangle.
<bookmark mark='above'/>Then pick two angles at the limit or above it. These do not.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: check for 70°: 70° + 20° = 90° is less than 180°, so the arms meet; 70° + 110° = 180°, so the arms do not meet

marks.meet: the first sum is written and a tick appears
marks.no: the second sum is written and a cross appears

narration: <bookmark mark='meet'/>Step four, check one pair each way for seventy degrees. Seventy plus twenty is ninety, which is less than one hundred and eighty, so the arms meet.
<bookmark mark='no'/>Seventy plus one hundred and ten is one hundred and eighty, so the arms do not meet.

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Any other angle below one hundred and eighty degrees minus the given angle makes a triangle.
<bookmark mark='i'/>For thirty degrees, forty and one hundred work. One hundred and fifty and one hundred and seventy do not.
<bookmark mark='ii'/>For seventy degrees, twenty and one hundred work. One hundred and ten and one hundred and thirty do not.
<bookmark mark='iii'/>For fifty four degrees, thirty and one hundred and twenty work. One hundred and twenty six and one hundred and fifty do not.
<bookmark mark='iv'/>For one hundred and forty four degrees, ten and thirty work. Thirty six and ninety do not.
